provenance: WS-7 T19 — every B1-B12 row resolved to a verdict, with the vocabulary extended so that a non-pass state is never readable as a pass. Verdicts are re-derivable from each row's own recorded numbers via scripts/perf-budget-verdicts.mjs verdictForRow.

specDivergence.issue: The spec contradicts itself about the ARM room-transition budget (B2), in four places.
specDivergence.supersession: D21-SUPERSESSION (spec :277-308) WITHDREW the ~1800 ms ARM ratification as unsound, with NO substitute adopted.
specDivergence.governingText: §4.6 B2 at :723 reads 'WITHDRAWN - NO DEFENSIBLE FIGURE'. This is the later and governing text and is what this manifest implements.
staleCopies: AC-045 at :1125-1131 — still says the ARM tier is 'ratified at ~1800 ms p95'.
T19's own acceptance line at :1368 — still says "B2's budget is already ratified at ~1800 ms by D21".
§9 ship gate at :1495 — still requires 'the ARM tier ratified at ~1800 ms'.
§4.6 verdict-vocabulary note at :739 and provenance note at :741 — both still describe B2 as 'ratified-but-not-directly-measured', which was true before the supersession and is not true now.
specDivergence.resolution: The supersession wins. No ~1800 ms figure appears as a live budget anywhere in this manifest, and B2 carries WITHDRAWN_UNMEASURED. An implementer following AC-045 literally would re-introduce a figure the owner withdrew. The vocabulary still contains RATIFIED_UNMEASURED so the pre-supersession state remains a defined, distinguishable state rather than an undefined one.
specDivergence.independentlyReconfirmed: This task found a THIRD, independent reason the derivation is unsound, beyond the supersession's two. scripts/arm-probe.mjs on this host measures x86 bench_ms 572-741 ms across five runs, against the 419.48 ms the 7.18x ratio was computed from. Had the relayed ARM figure of 3012.39 ms held, the ratio against this host is about 4.67x, not 7.18x. A CPU-only ratio that varies by host cannot be carried onto a render-bound transition budget. See arm-probe.json rows.B12.crossChecks.

vocabulary.note: Only `pass` satisfies a budget. The other six are distinct honest states, and `verdictForRow` has no code path returning `pass` without comparing a measured percentile against a numeric budget.

rows.reason: BREACH, and the verdict is over-determined while the figure is not. The 250 ms x86-only tier is exceeded by every one of the 24 per-rate p95 values measured across five runs (1x: 207-597 ms; 4x: 4875-13781 ms; 6x: 7238 ms), so no plausible sample could make this row pass. The exact figure is NOT ratified: only 1 of 5 runs ever reached the 6x rate, so the 12 raw samples above come from that single run, and plan v1 §3.7 item 2 forbids ratifying a number from one run. rawSamplesMs is therefore the single surviving 6x sample set, and `ratifiedFigureMs` is null rather than quoting 7238 ms as the settled figure.

rows.note: This is the DASHBOARD leg of the transition loop. terminal-perf.spec.ts:620-622 states outright that `elapsed` is 't0 -> the DASHBOARD marker only'; the markets leg is timed separately as marketsMarkerMs. Both legs are reported in the changelog because they are different measurements.

rows.reason: The ~1800 ms ratification is WITHDRAWN as unsound (D21 supersession, :277-308) and NO replacement was substituted, so there is no figure for a sample to be measured against and no comparison is possible. It was derived as 250 ms x 7.18x, which is invalid on the supersession's two independent grounds: the 7.18x ratio is a CPU-only benchmark while the transition is render-bound (route 22 ms vs render 1823 ms avg, per the T2 diagnostic), and the 250 ms input was a max-of-5-warming-samples figure rather than a percentile. A third, independent ground was found by this task: the x86 leg of that ratio does not reproduce on this host. ARM room-transition cost is genuinely unknown and only a direct on-device sample can close it.
rows.closure: Requires a direct on-device ARM64 room-transition sample. No x86 proxy can produce one — that is the whole argument at scripts/arm-probe.mjs:2-6. No ARM64 device is attached to this host (platform=win32-x64), so this row cannot be advanced here.

rows.rawSamplesRef: apps/dashboard/perf/ram-ceiling-gate.json rawSamplesMb (17 samples in the recorded run)
rows.reason: Graduated from UNMEASURED to a measured peak. The 2048 MB ceiling is frozen and is NOT raised to accommodate a room (T19's bisect line, spec :1370). Two valid runs measured 385.5 MB and 372.1 MB; the higher is reported. Peak is 18.8% of the ceiling. Measured as the summed working set of the whole vite process tree (node + esbuild + conhost), NOT the browser tab's JS heap — the manifest's jsHeapMb of ~30 MB is one tab and is not the stack.

Vendor-reported and not independently verified: 8-29 MB, 29-121M params, CQ2 2-bit, android-arm64, peak_ram_mb 28.5. T13 obtained and digest-pinned the artifact but did not measure its runtime footprint, so this stays UNVERIFIED. A vendor claim is not a measurement.

This row carries two separable claims and they do not stand or fall together. (1) CHECKSUM IDENTITY — CORROBORATED: this independent x86 host computed bench_checksum=2095.419, matching the owner-relayed value exactly across five runs, so the bench is deterministic across machines as claimed. (2) THE 7.18x RATIO — NOT REPRODUCED: the owner relayed x86 bench_ms 419.48 and this host measures 572-741 ms across five runs, outside a 10% band; had the relayed ARM 3012.39 ms held, the ratio against this host is about 4.67x. Recording a single token here would be a lie in one direction or the other, so the row records which half is which. This is a material finding for B2: it is a third independent ground for the D21 supersession's withdrawal.
